body: **2026-11-17-standing-live-rig** — ~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing gained its except: the test-only standing live rig reads the trust selector's place, the input box and modal dialogs as closed words only, raw frames local and gitignored. This chunk's S0 runs a live `viola verify` on that rig and its sixth run reads whether the trust dialog shows, so any new screen read must stay inside that exception or the compiled signatures.

**2026-11-13-verify-readiness-on-the-input-box** — ~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing widened the compiled signatures to footer literals, the input box's rule and prompt rows (opening char only) and modal literals, as a boundary widening the founder ratified. The sixth run's "first settled frame is no trust dialog" post-condition has to read the screen through those compiled modal/input-box signatures only, never the text after them.

**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — A `verify` stopped by Ctrl-C/TERM prints no step line and no summary, only the `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` pair, exits 1, pinned by the stop table in `tests/cli_verify.rs`; the stop path adds no time bound. The sixth run's "remove its own record on every exit path" has to land inside this stop path without changing the pair, the exit or the no-step-line rule (contract/interrupted-verify/*, contract/viola-verify/interrupted-pair).

**2026-10-20-t06-58-31-wrap** — The interrupted pair's wording was made the founder's own (its provisional mark superseded). The pair's text is fixed; the record clean-up on a stop must not reword or add to it.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (strict-modes refusals as scope entities; their text; witnesses and pinned pairs; unstattable home) — `viola verify` over a home failing strict modes refuses before its log opens: exit 1, the home-state pair, `hint:` last, no step line, no summary (`refuse_home`, `update_stamps`'s `StampsError::StrictModes`); witnesses `verify_refuses_a_widened_ledger_before_any_step` and `verify_under_a_regular_file_refuses_the_home` in `tests/cli_verify.rs`, pair pinned by literal. Rows contract/start-refusal/home-strict-modes, decision/strict-modes-refusal-before-any-write and decision/unstattable-home-is-strict-modes-refusal come from here: a sixth run, the record writer, and a 23rd ledger row must not write anything (the trust record included) before that check.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (strict-modes Windows arms retired; a11y cases' CI home; the Linux-only platform line; tui boundary on openpty; cli SGR checks without Windows arms) — `verify_under_a_regular_file_refuses_the_home`'s oracle is the home-state pair alone; every a11y case runs in the `coverage` suite on the one `ubuntu-latest` leg under `gate --require coverage,doctest`; the platform is Linux only; the TUI is hosted on openpty alone; the colour decision has no Windows VT branch. The writer's file I/O (lock, atomic replace, read-back) and the new `cli_verify` cases need a Linux path only, with nothing skipped.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (a refused socket directory at the start) — `viola run` and a `viola revive` start over a failing socket directory refuse with exit 1 before any snapshot, bind or child; the fixed-message `unable:` / `hint:` pair; the directory left as found (contract/start-refusal/socket-dir, decision/socket-dir-refusal-before-any-frame). It is the precedent that a refusal leaves the file system as found: verify's record writer has to give the same guarantee for the trust record on a refused or failed write.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — Records the first live reading of the takeover clause as supplemental and never gating (decision/live-readings-never-gate). This chunk's live S0 `viola verify` stamp is the same kind of reading: it informs and never gates CI.

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** — The second live takeover reading, on a real `claude` with the founder's own key, also supplemental and never gating. It is the precedent for a live reading under the founder's cap with no agent typing a key, which matches S0's `keys: none`.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** (cli checks on std::process::Command and literal pins; the §8 verification lines; the cli tooling contracts) — Output discipline is checked by `std::process::Command` with each fixed string pinned by a literal (was trycmd/assert_cmd); every fixed CLI string, hints and result lines included, is pinned (decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned*, decision/cli-a11y-by-literal-tests). The sixth run's `[NN/NN] … pass|fail` step line and the new row's closed words need literal pins, and the step-count sweep has to move every pinned spelling of the count.

**2026-10-16-remove-the-browser-leg** — The cli/tui a11y cases became ordinary nextest cases in the `test` job's `coverage` suite, with no a11y stage, driver or suite value of their own; a `gate --require coverage,doctest` breach fails the build; `#[ignore]` is banned. The new verify-probe cases join that suite, with none ignored and no retries (decision/a11y-runs-in-existing-test-suites, decision/a11y-gate-breach-fails-build, decision/zero-flakiness).

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** — CLI output-discipline evidence reports inside the CI `coverage` suite under `gate --require coverage,doctest`. This is where the `cli_verify` changes this chunk puts in the gate block report.

**2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates** — `ci.yml` is the one push/PR workflow carrying a11y; the scheduled `nightly.yml` carries no a11y step (decision/a11y-ci-github-actions). Any new verify case belongs in `ci.yml`'s test job.

**2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — Mutation over the CLI output-discipline invariants moved to the epoch-boundary audit, with no per-chunk gate. This matches the scope's "no mutation run".

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (the census of error writers; a peer's refusal screened to a code word; `unknown`'s detail) — `error_bodies_each_name_a_writer_and_a_witness_that_stand`, `product_error_writers_are_each_named` and `thiserror_messages_interpolate_nothing` hold every error body. `is_code_word` defines the code-word format. `unknown` (exit 14) is the hint carve-out. A record writer that adds error types (file absent, unreadable, a link, not the expected JSON, oversize) must name a writer and a witness, interpolate nothing, and report its closed words in code-word form.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (one hint per code) — `no_two_codes_share_a_hint`, `no_hint_names_release` and the exit-cause table in `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` hold every code to its own hint. Any new refusal code or hint the probe's closed words introduce must pass them.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — ~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver and ~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human dropped the budget pause from their lists of time bounds. These rows list every bound viola holds. If the sixth run's settle wait or the writer's 3-attempt lock adds a bound, it must fall on verify's own child, never on a human key.

**2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed** — ~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human and ~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver dropped the status-line deadline, which gives the current wording of both time-bound rows the chunk rests on.

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** — A held dialog always returns to the human: the hold bounds only the driver. This is the precedent for the scope's rule that when the CLI does not honour the record, the trust dialog stays the human's.
**2026-11-01-t02-46-44-wrap** — The founder kept the a11y tier at `Standard (1)` (decision/a11y-tier-standard). The chunk adds no surface that re-opens the tier.

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — Built the colour decision (NO_COLOR, TERM, COLORTERM, stdout's terminal state; truecolor/256/16 depth) and the rule that each SGR span sits beside its word, with `unable`/`fail` never coloured. A 23rd row whose stamp turns 22-row stamps `unverified-cli` on the board, and a new verify step reading `fail`, are both bound by these rules.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** — A passed `viola revive` enters the same TUI passthrough boundary as `viola run`, the single vendor-content zone (decision/single-vendor-content-boundary). This chunk changes nothing of `run`/`revive`, and verify's interactive children are not part of that boundary.

**2026-11-12T03-23-49-rows** — The master text became the rows this chunk is bound by, each verified against the code. Every expected amendment (the child set of five becoming six, the bounded `~/.claude.json` exception for verify's own record) is written as a row change against those handles.

Adds the 23rd relied capability-ledger row in viola-agent-claude: the claude CLI honours a per-project trust record (hasTrustDialogAccepted) another process wrote into the config file its child reads.
Adds its viola verify probe as a SIXTH interactive verify run: it writes the trust record for its own OS-temp dir, expects the child's first settled frame to show no trust dialog, then removes only its own record on every exit path.
Builds the record writer once (lock when free, atomic replace, read-back, at most 3 attempts), where the next entry's product write can use it; the fake agent now reads the record, not argv --trusted-root alone.
Re-runs the step-count sweep the sixth run moves over every spelling of the count, and stamps the row with one live viola verify (S0) on the 2.1.325 install under the rig's private config.
Changes nothing of viola run or revive; the product's own trust write is not part of this chunk.
viola verify output gains a sixth interactive run: its step lines (the step-line contract) and the step count every printed form of verify's progress carries move from five interactive runs to six.

The new probe's row prints a closed word for what it could not do (config file absent, unreadable, a link, not the expected JSON, or oversize), never pass; it prints fail when the CLI does not honour the record. These are fixed verify output strings pinned by literal.
verify's summary prints what proves verify's own trust record is gone after the run; a fixed line in verify's output.

An interrupted verify (Ctrl-C or the stop) during the sixth run still removes verify's own record and prints the interrupted pair and exit 1 unchanged; the plan says what a SIGKILLed verify leaves and that the stop removes it.
verify's output must not carry the OS-temp dir path or the config file path it writes into; paths are not carried, and any byte printed from a path or reason is escaped as a C0/C1 control character.

The probe's post-condition reads only the child's first settled frame for the trust dialog signature; no screen-content parsing beyond signatures, and the check never inspects claude content otherwise.

The probe's control (record withheld, the dialog read) and post-condition are proved on the fake agent in the existing test suites; each control fires with its --timeout S, waits are bounded under the 20 s lint, and time bounds fall on the driver, never the human.
A change to the fake agent's trust reading or screens puts the cli_verify tests in the gate block; they run with no skips, no retries, zero flakiness.
Live readings never gate: the live S0 verify stamps the ledger row but no CI check depends on it; the tests' shared stamp and CI stay green with the 23rd row relied.
verify's refusals before any start (home strict-modes failure, socket directory failure) are unchanged by the sixth run and still come before any write, now including the trust-record write.
No SGR in plain modes and no colour on refusal or failure words: the new probe row's closed word and fail word print uncoloured, with the word carrying the state.
No spinners and linear static output: the sixth run's progress prints as static step lines like the other five.

each new fixed CLI string is pinned by its literal in a test and its copy comes from design
each new test runs under the CI gate with no skips, no retries and zero flakiness, its failures nextest failures

body: The viola list board, its captions, colour, stale rows, NAME truncation and the unwrapped separator: the chunk prints nothing on the board.
viola revive refusals, revive --json documents and revive --list: nothing of revive changes here.
viola run TUI passthrough rows (human keystrokes, focus/mouse/resize sequences, own terminal bytes, feed panic): viola run is not changed.
viola link and unlink, plugin install, and viola --help rows: no verb is added or changed besides verify.
MCP frame tools, hook event and dialog calls, frame verb refusals and instance-unreachable details: the chunk touches no frame channel.
viola send and viola wait output and refusals, and the dialog hold: the chunk sends nothing and answers no dialog.
Screen-reader targets, manual Orca and keyboard passes, and visual design rows (amber, bold): no manual pass is owed by this chunk.

**2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows** (R8 prefix rule + identity floor, explicit child cwd, viola-side program resolution) — made R8 a `CLAUDE*` prefix strip with an 11-name identity floor and the `config.json` `claude_env_keep` pass-list, set the child cwd explicitly and had viola resolve the child program itself. Why it matters: S0 runs verify under the rig's private config through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` kept by `claude_env_keep` (the file the record goes into depends on whether that name survives the strip), and the sixth run sets its child's cwd to its own OS-temp dir.

**2026-09-26-local-linux-pre-push-gate** (`FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` test seam) — the first ratified fake-agent env seam, `fake-agent` feature only, a boundary widening. Precedent for this chunk: the fake agent must read the trust record from the config file, so any new fake-agent input needs to fit the seam rules (`decision/fake-agent-test-seams`, `decision/test-seams-not-configuration`) rather than add a new env name.

**2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order** (tempfile `persist` snapshot writer) — replaced atomic-write-file (BSD-3-Clause, outside `deny.toml`) with tempfile `persist` through ONE shared helper in `viola_state::fs` (mode set before any byte). This is the reason behind `decision/tempfile-snapshot-writer` and `decision/atomic-replaced-state-files`: the record writer's atomic replace of `.claude.json` must go through those helpers, not carry its own temp + rename.

**2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate** (the second fake-agent test seam `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC`) — two ratified seams now, each a founder-ratified boundary widening. A third env seam would need ratification. The founder later refused one for the fake agent (see 2026-10-16), so the fake agent's record read should take the config path it already gets (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `~/.claude.json`), not a new seam.

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** (ledger rows, `viola verify`'s probe, the stamps envelope) — created the closed ledger in `viola_agent_claude::ledger`, the "verified only when every row passes" rule, `viola verify` with its `ledger/probes/<pid>/` drop-guarded dirs, the stamps envelope and its one writer `update_stamps`. This is the register the 23rd row extends.

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** (the version gate placed and split by crate) — split the gate three ways: Claude parsing, rows and verdict in the pure `viola-agent-claude` (no `viola-state` edge), the spawn in the root bin, stamps I/O in `viola_state::stamps`. This is the precedent for the scope's inferred split of the record writer: the JSON shape on the Claude side, the lock, atomic replace and read-back on a side both `verify` and the later `run` reach (`decision/agent-claude-pure`).

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** (the hidden `hook --capture` arm, founder-ratified exceptions) — verify's transient unwrapped probe children and the capture arm were ratified as boundary widenings and named the only exception to [Plugin Scope]. The sixth run is another transient unwrapped child, and its record write is a new widening of what verify touches outside the viola home.

**2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness** — harness homes are stamped by `viola verify` against the fake agent at boot, root homes by `stamped_home`, and `run --local-live` is the one real-`claude` verify home. Why it matters: once the row is relied, the scope's claim that "the tests' shared stamp and CI stay green" rests on these stamp paths and on `contract_ledger_probes`' stamped sets carrying the new row.

**2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records** — introduced the partial readiness gate on an unverified CLI (`decision/partial-gate-on-unverified-cli`). This is the behaviour every 22-row-stamped home falls back to once the 23rd row is relied and its stamp reads unverified (the scope's "stamps go stale").

**2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id** (decisions on the six-row stamp, the strict stamps read) — `run`'s version gate reads stamps through `read_stamps_strict`. A refusal is `cli_verified:false` with `parse-rejected{ledger-stamps, strict-modes-failed}` (`decision/version-gate-strict-stamps-read`). `stamped_home` stamps at a recorded version. This is the stale-stamp path the plan must name.

**2026-10-04-readiness-gate-and-timing-constants** — made vt100 the pure `viola_agent_claude::screen::Screen`, a pre-send gate only, with modal signatures as compiled literal lists (`decision/vt100-readiness-gate`, `decision/vt100-screen-model`). The sixth run's post-condition ("first settled frame is no trust dialog") reads the same screen model and the modal literal.

**2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes** (screen signatures compiled, ten ledger rows, verify's interactive runs) — compiled `SIGNATURES` with the modal `Yes, I trust this folder`. It added Run A (untrusted, OS-temp dir, killed, no key into the dialog) and Run B (trusted). Measured on 2.1.288: trust is inherited from a trusted parent. The sixth run is a Run A twin over a fresh OS-temp dir, and its control is Run A's own reading. The inherited-trust fact is a trap: the temp dir must have no trusted ancestor.

**2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes** (registry rows for verify's interactive runs and screen fixtures) — gave the fake agent `--trusted-root` (argv, no env), Run A's OS-temp `viola-verify-*` dir via `tempfile`, verify's spawn-pair count and the `Screen.<phase>` fixtures. Per the scope's corrected premise, the fake agent decides trust from `--trusted-root` alone, and that is what this chunk changes. A new run moves the spawn-pair count and the probe-dir registry.

**2026-10-05-dialog-rows-and-re-probe** — added Runs C and D (four interactive runs), the probe-dir list, and the spawn pairs going from four to six. It is the pattern for the bookkeeping a new interactive run carries: `diagnostics/` spawn pairs, the probe dir list, `[Plugin Scope]`'s transient-children count and CI's fake-agent modes.

**2026-10-05-permission-end-to-end** — kept a question first raised by PermissionRequest `null` because its body has no ledger row, and adding one costs a new row, its probe and a re-stamp. This is the source of `decision/permission-request-question-stays-null`. Its "Nth row" count moves when this chunk takes the 23rd row (it reads 22nd today).

**2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows** — set the precedent that adding rows makes a stamp of the older id set read unverified, and that a Run B widening needs the founder's own live answer. It also re-recorded only one version, which left another drift-only. Both are relevant to the 23rd row staling every 22-row stamp and to S0 stamping 2.1.325 alone.

**2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host** (the long-paste frame as measured beside typed text and between two pairs) — the founder ruled the limit that a CLI shape no `send` relies on needs no probe (`decision/no-probe-for-unrelied-shapes`). This chunk's shape is relied on by the later product write, so it takes a row with a probe, not that limit.

**2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host** (the identity floor's Linux reading) — recorded the CLAUDE* names a hook and a session are handed, names only, and that the floor stays at eleven (`decision/identity-floor-eleven-names`, `decision/env-strip-names-only`). Relevant to keeping `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` through `claude_env_keep` for S0 and to the rule that the strip reads names, never values.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — set `GATE_MAX_WAIT` to 8.5 s, validated per version by the quiet-period row (`decision/gate-timings-compiled`), and raised the fake agent's hold cap. A settled-frame read in the sixth run uses these compiled timings. Its standing trap: a case reading a verified literal-less screen through a clock that never advances waits forever.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (the snapshot's `cwd` and the child's second cwd source) — gave the child a second cwd source, the revived snapshot's `cwd` (`decision/child-cwd-explicit` except). That except is the shape for naming another cwd source. The sixth run sets its own temp dir, and its record key is the cwd, or the cwd's git root inside a repository.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** (four crossings ratified by the founder) — writing a code-bearing file the CLI reads (the settings override) was a boundary widening the founder ratified live. Standing rule: a widening he answered before the wrap still halts there as one card. The record writer into the CLI's own config file is the same class of crossing, and its expected amendments ride the wrap's answer card.

**2026-10-10-budget-governor** (the instance check before any log, on both arms) — measured that opening a log narrows an existing home to 0700, so a check after it passes a widened home. This is the source of `decision/strict-check-before-log-open` and `decision/refused-check-writes-no-line`. Any new verify path that reads home files must keep its check before the log.

**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — verify's dirs are removed when it passes, fails, or is stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM, through drop guards that remove only what that run created, never by a pattern or a listing. A stopped run kills its child with no key, writes no stamp and exits 1 `interrupted`. SIGKILL and a crash leave the dirs to be removed by hand. This is the model for "verify removes ONLY its own record on every exit path" and for saying what a SIGKILLed verify leaves (`decision/verify-removes-only-own-dirs`).

**2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row** — took the ledger to eighteen rows. The step lines `[NN/MM]` take `MM` from the relied count, older-id stamps read unverified, and "every home stamped before reads `cli_verified:false` until its next verify". The new paste was ratified as a boundary widening of the verify child set. This is the template for the 23rd row's step-count sweep and stale-stamp statement.

**2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows** — introduced `LedgerRow::relied()` and "a version is verified only when every relied row reads pass" (`decision/version-verified-all-relied-rows`, `contract/ledger-stamps/verified-version`). It also added Run B's probe `--settings`, the probe document verify writes into its own dir. The new row joins the relied set and moves `MM`.

**2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows** (the resume row, Run E and /compact listed) — Run E made verify FIVE interactive runs. It was a boundary widening ratified by the founder's own answer, it runs last in a guarded 0700 dir, and it depends on Run B (`decision/verify-run-e-resumes-run-b-first-session`). This is the direct precedent for the sixth run: its order relative to A–E, its own dir and its widening card.

**2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows** (Run E's resources and a killed PTY child's exit status) — a new run adds a spawn pair (seven then), a probe-dir entry and a fixture stem, and stamps the committed set via `contract_ledger_probes`. A killed interactive child closes with a `child_exit_status`. These are the registry rows the sixth run moves.

That ruling constrains how the fake agent learns which config file to read for the record.

The step lines moved, older stamps read unverified, and the committed set was re-stamped. The same sweep (step lines, `--record`, fixtures, the fake agent replay) applies to the 23rd row.

CI artifact upload, retention and the detail-file upload rules: the chunk adds no upload.

Adds the 23rd relied capability-ledger row in the Claude adapter: the claude CLI honours a per-project trust record (hasTrustDialogAccepted under the CLI's own project key) that another process wrote into the config file its child reads.
Gives the row its viola verify probe: a sixth interactive verify run over its own fresh OS-temp dir that writes that trust record, expects the child's first settled frame to be no trust dialog, and removes only its own record after the run; a control with the record withheld must read the dialog.
Builds the trust-record writer once (lock when free, atomic replace, read-back, at most 3 attempts), placed where the later product write in viola run can reach it, and makes the fake agent read the record from the config file rather than decide trust from argv alone.
Re-runs the step-count sweep the sixth run moves over every spelling of the count, and stamps the row with one live viola verify (S0, plus one spare S0-2) on the 2.1.325 install under the live rig's private config; no capability is claimed.

The capability ledger and the unverified-CLI gate: a 23rd relied row with its own verify probe; once it is relied every 22-row stamp reads unverified, so the stamps verify writes and the version gate's read of them are reached, while the tests' shared stamp and CI must stay green.

The ratified verify child set grows from five to six: the sixth interactive run is spawned directly like the others, over its own OS-temp probe directory, and its effects stay in that directory except the one bounded record.

Verify never types into or answers a dialog: the sixth run sends no dialog byte and pastes only its own ratified literals; it decides the trust dialog's absence only by reading the screen against compiled literals and signatures.

The rule that viola writes nothing under the Claude home or into Claude's config (~/.claude.json): verify's own trust record becomes its one bounded exception; the product's write is not amended in by this chunk.

The record's form and target: key is the cwd's git root inside a repository, else the cwd; hasTrustDialogAccepted alone; the file is <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json when the child's environment keeps that variable, else ~/.claude.json.

The writer's race rule and replace path: take the CLI's lock when free, replace atomically, read back, at most 3 attempts; it meets the rule that one shared helper replaces files and the rule that state readers never write.

The writer's refusals: a config file absent, unreadable, a symlink, not the JSON expected or oversize leaves nothing written, and the probe's row reads a closed word for what it could not do, never pass; its read of the config is bounded and keeps the default JSON depth limit.

Removal of verify's record: only its own record, never another project's, on every exit path the run reaches; the plan states what a SIGKILLed verify leaves and that the stop removes it; the probe directory is removed by its drop guard and probe artefacts stay owner-only and transient.

Writer placement across the crate boundary: the Claude adapter does no file I/O and the state crate is Claude-free, so the record's JSON shape sits on the Claude side and the lock, atomic replace and read-back on a side both verify and the later run reach; the sync crates stay tokio-free.
The probe must be able to fail: when the CLI does not honour the record the row reads fail; the product then never writes the record and the trust dialog stays the human's to answer.

The fake agent's test seam changes: it decides trust by reading the record from the same config file and key the writer used, not argv --trusted-root alone, so both the post-condition and the control can fail on it; a change to its screens or trust reading puts the cli_verify job in the gate block.

The child's environment: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR reaches the verify child only through the claude_env_keep config value, while the inherited CLAUDE credentials and parent identity variables stay stripped and the process-start line's env_kept field reports it.

The live round: S0 is one live verify by path on the 2.1.325 install (7 claude starts: 1 print probe, 6 interactive) under the live rig's private config seeded by seed_config, child isolated from the user's config, credentials copy transient; keys: none into any dialog or box, the rig keying only its own pty; stop: Ctrl-C into its own pty or a no-key group kill; the real CLI runs only locally, never in CI.
The founder's real ~/.claude.json is read only by the mark witness, and verify's summary prints what proves its record is gone after the run, holding no paths, pids or identity values.
The owed rootOnly reading: what makes the CLI count only the git root's record is read from the installed CLI's strings where reachable without a start, else named unmeasured.
Verify's accepted residuals widen by one run: the trusted-run risk, real-CLI transcripts and echo-probe residuals now also cover the sixth run and its pre-written record.

Tests and controls: no mutation run; each control fired with a named --timeout; control and sweep ids at most 16 characters; a waiting test bounded under the 20 s lint; the session sets no timer and ends every process it starts.
